clue.text: A landlord normally is willing to help

definitions.meaning: a landlord provides rooms to live in, so in the providing-lodging sense that is what a landlord usually is
obliging, keen to do others a favour

explanation.surface: Most landlords, the clue claims, are happy to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the word in its literal sense of providing lodgings; the second is the everyday sense of obliging.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obliging bends to suit others, the everyday sense of the word.

clue.text: A way to overcome a reduced noise of clock in movement

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overcome puts the first pieces on top of the rest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a clock's noise is a tick

explanation.surface: A clockmaker describes a shortened tick in a watch's movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like the clock's works, but the definition describes something not fixed in position; 'reduced' cuts TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astatic has no tendency to settle in a fixed position, so it is prone to shifting.

clue.text: Constellation called initially by English name The Bull

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the word called is used

parts.note: Taurus is the Latin name of the zodiac sign the Bull

explanation.surface: A star group is said to be named after the Bull by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'The Bull' looks like the constellation's title; it gives TAURUS, completing the name of the southern constellation of the Centaur.
explanation.definitionFit: The Centaur is a large group of stars in the southern sky, named in Latin.

clue.text: Gosh -about to chew something like beef

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes round the word for chew

parts.note: my! is an exclamation like gosh!
to chew food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims before chewing on a steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is flesh, and a substantial, flesh-like food is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Meaning to dominate, Cicero's last part of speech gets attention

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the word Cicero's is taken

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A Roman orator's closing words command the audience's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meaning' is a link word; the possessive 's of Cicero's is no letter, so his last letter is O.
explanation.definitionFit: To lord it over others, or to bully, is to dominate them.

clue.text: African country laid out along central part of coast

indicators.note: laid out means arranged afresh, so the letters of the word are reordered
central part of means the middle letter of coast is taken

explanation.surface: An African nation stretches out along the middle of a coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' rearranges ALONG to ANGOL; the middle letter of 'coast' is A.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-west African republic on the Atlantic, capital Luanda, is a nation of that continent.

clue.text: Moist rice cooked in equal measures

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Damp rice is cooked using equal measures of water and grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges MOIST RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric means having equal dimensions or measurements.

clue.text: Part of roof beginning to buckle in high wind

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the word for a strong wind

parts.note: a gale is a high wind

indicators.note: beginning to means just the first letter of buckle

explanation.surface: A section of roof starts to give way in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to buckle' gives B, which goes 'in' GALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular end wall beneath a pitched roof is a feature of the roof structure.

clue.text: Where synod holds belief not normally acceptable

indicators.note: holds means the letters are contained within the words where synod

explanation.surface: A church council meeting somewhere maintains an unorthodox belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' looks like a synod holding a view, but it signals that the answer sits within 'wHERE SYnod'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion contrary to orthodox doctrine is a belief not normally accepted by the church.

clue.text: Delay with NT upset translator of Bible

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the usual abbreviation for New Testament

explanation.surface: A hold-up caused by a disarranged New Testament annoys a Bible translator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DELAY plus NT; the NT looks like a nod to the Bible in the surface, but here it is just two letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tyndale made the first printed English translation of the New Testament in the 1520s.

clue.text: What's said when going for a bargain, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: a bargain is a good buy

explanation.surface: A shopper describes the words exchanged at a bargain counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' means GOOD BUY (a bargain) said out loud gives the parting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is the word people say on leaving.

clue.text: Obsequious type — a dramatist's most original character in play

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the word for play

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

indicators.note: the most original, that is the first, letter of the word dramatist's

explanation.surface: A flatterer is held up as a playwright's freshest creation on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most original character' is not a role in a play but the first letter, D, of 'dramatist's'; A and D go 'in' TOY (play).
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns on those above, the very picture of an obsequious person.

clue.text: Darling without love before? Prospects are excellent here

indicators.note: without means the letter for love is dropped from the word for darling

parts.note: a darling is one's beloved
love is O, a zero score in tennis
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A sweetheart without affection asks about prospects, which look good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospects' looks like future chances but means views: the definition describes a turret or summerhouse built for the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo or roofed gallery is put up to command a fine view, so the views from it are excellent.

clue.text: Brainy British gathered in corn, perhaps

indicators.note: gathered in means the abbreviation is taken inside, as a harvest is gathered into the barn

parts.note: corn is an example of a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A clever Briton is pictured among the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual person relies on the brain, as the adjective says.

clue.text: Enjoyable time on island with a dancing-girl?

parts.note: to have a ball is to have a great time
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland, an island

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker has fun on an island with a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts BALL above ERIN; the question mark marks the definition as describing a female ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ballet dancer is a girl who dances classically.

clue.text: Rich gal has abandoned economy

indicators.note: has abandoned means the girl's word is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: economy means thrift, frugality

explanation.surface: A wealthy girl gives up thrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' sits beside a gal in the surface as if describing her wealth; it is the definition, as in a rich, plummy voice or rich flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich voice or flavour is full and mellow, like a ripe fruit-laden wine.

clue.text: Part in Mediterranean style of architecture on view, say

parts.note: Ionian, or Ionic, is a classical order of Greek architecture

indicators.note: say tells the solver that the word is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: to see is to have in view

explanation.surface: Part of a Mediterranean building is shown off in classical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mediterranean style' reads as one phrase but splits: the definition ends at 'Mediterranean'. The Ionic order is also called Ionian, and 'say' signals the spoken form of the word meaning to have on view.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of water between Greece and southern Italy is an arm of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Unrivalled specimen is unchosen, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means the letters are in odd, unexpected order

explanation.surface: A peerless example has oddly never been picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges UNCHOSEN; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a person or thing without equal, a paragon.

clue.text: Hurry back puffing?

definitions.meaning: a pad worn at the back of a skirt to puff it out, a Victorian fashion

explanation.definitionFit: A busy scurry is a hurry; the Victorian frame padding a skirt behind is the dress sense.

clue.text: Bachelor Maxim turns over in bed

indicators.note: turns over means the word for maxim is read backwards

parts.note: a maxim is a motto

explanation.surface: A single man named Maxim tosses and turns in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns over' reverses MOTTO to OTTOM. 'bed' is a riverbed or seabed, the lowest part.
explanation.definitionFit: A riverbed or seabed is the ground beneath the water, its base.

clue.text: This sort of cone may overflow when it's hot

definitions.text: This sort of cone may overflow when it's hot

parts.words: This sort of cone may overflow when it's hot
parts.note: reads like an ice-cream cone melting in the heat, but means the mountain cone that pours out lava when active

explanation.definitionFit: A mountain built of ejected lava erupts when hot, so its cone is of the fiery-mountain type.

clue.text: Brilliant star in cloak everyone turned up to see

parts.note: a cape is a cloak

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for everyone is read upwards

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A star turns up in a cloak for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ALL to LLA in this down clue; 'in' and 'to see' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the constellation Auriga is one of the most brilliant in the sky.

clue.text: Bookmaker making old woman most profit

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman

indicators.note: most means all but the last letter of the word for profit

parts.note: gain means profit

explanation.surface: A betting shop owner makes the most profit from an old lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' looks like a bookie but means the author of a book of the Bible; 'most' trims GAIN to GAI.
explanation.definitionFit: The prophet credited with a short Old Testament book is a maker of that book.

clue.text: Put it on board before fare is collected?

definitions.text: Put it on board before fare is collected?

parts.words: Put it on board before fare is collected?
parts.note: reads like a bus passenger before the conductor takes the fare, but board is a table and fare is food: plates and cutlery are laid before the meal

explanation.definitionFit: Plates, dishes and cutlery are laid on a dining table before food is served.

clue.text: Consecrate bishop? Not so

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
less means not so much, as in less hot meaning not so hot

explanation.surface: A bishop is asked whether he will consecrate something and declines.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanctify or hallow something is to consecrate it.

clue.text: Make an impression and secure the post?

definitions.meaning: to press a mark into something
a postage label pays for and so secures the sending of mail

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing a die leaves a mark, and the adhesive postage label pays for a letter.

clue.text: Weapon English used in fight

indicators.note: used in means the abbreviation is placed inside the word for fight

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do

explanation.surface: An Englishman takes a weapon into a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pointed throwing or thrusting pole is a weapon.

clue.text: An eye, maybe, for starting business

definitions.meaning: the eye of a needle is an example of a hole or gap
the launch of a shop or firm

explanation.definitionFit: A gap such as a needle's eye is a hole, and a launch of a business is its first day of trading.

clue.text: Such an implement unties knotted line

indicators.note: knotted means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Untying a knotted line needs the right tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knotted' rearranges UNTIES with L (line).
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool is an example of an implement.

clue.text: Armed expedition repulsed after game was finished off

definitions.text: Armed expedition repulsed after game was finished off

parts.words: Armed expedition repulsed after game was finished off
parts.note: recalls the legend that Sir Francis Drake insisted on finishing his game of bowls at Plymouth before sailing out to defeat the invading fleet of 1588

explanation.walkthrough: The story goes that Drake, told the enemy fleet was sighted, finished his game of bowls first; bowls is a lawn game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip II's invasion fleet of 1588 was a military expedition beaten back by the English navy.
